summary: Dynalene cooling problems forced an emergency warmup of ComCam (48V PDU/REBPS shut off, cryotels off, controlled warm-up of cryo stage). No FRACAS ticket in the glycol/Dynalene catalog is dated exactly Aug 7 2024; FRACAS-229 (Dynalene System Controller Failure), filed 2 days later on Aug 9 2024, is the closest matching ticket and may be the after-the-fact writeup of this same event -- treat the FRACAS linkage as a best guess, not confirmed.

Multi-system crisis reported live during the CCR2-ORR1 review: glycol filter clog triggered an emergency trip, ComCam was being warmed up, Simonyi was stuck, and LSSTCam was 'hanging in there.' No matching ticket was found in the glycol/Dynalene FRACAS catalog for this date -- this appears to be a gap in FRACAS reporting rather than an untagged ticket; worth confirming with the team whether a ticket was ever filed.

PCS Chiller2 E2 Compressor 1 failure (CB11 breaker tripped from a shorted FAN2 fan/heater unit). Camera team shut down HV bias, all CCDs, and all REBs in stages to protect the cold plate; cold plate and cryo plate temperatures spiked (REB temps nearly hit the 25C critical limit). Root cause (failed FAN2 unit) found and replaced the next day (~Mar 21); PCS chiller was then deliberately restarted/reset at a conservative high setpoint (-10C) and low flow rate (1 gal/min) to avoid thermally shocking the cold plate.

Glycol flow to the camera cooling system degraded starting ~May 5 (flow dropped to 1.7 gpm vs 3 gpm minimum requirement, PCS glycol output temp spiked to 44C) due to a clogged filter at the PCS chiller, worsening through May 7 when FRACAS-383/384 were opened. Camera cold plate/REBs were powered down and the PCS was taken out of operation; the May 8 morning tailgate confirmed camera cooling had only been restarted the prior afternoon (~4:15pm) and was still not at operating temperature. Filter was physically cleared on May 10, 2026.
